mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in every one of the last four weekly means (-43.3, -41.0, -39.7, -36.1), and this own-series momentum is self-propagating: each week of improvement widens the pool of reopened retail capacity, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -43.3 at t-3w to -36.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: gradual reopening with monotone weekly improvement
failure_condition: The 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -40.03, the trailing four-week mean, i.e. direction_4w is not '+'.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -40 marks the point at which discretionary trips resume rather than only essential errands; once that threshold is crossed, retail footfall follows with a two-week lag because trip planning precedes browsing and purchase.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -40.0 (it printed -40.7 at t-1w and -37.1 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -43.3 at t-3w to -37.1 at t-0w, crossing -40.0 in the most recent week
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT is above -40.0, the RETAIL_REC mean two weeks later is not higher than in weeks where TRANSIT is below -40.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of RESIDENTIAL falling (12.4 to 11.4) while PARKS rises (-33.9 to -20.6) shows households converting home-bound time into out-of-home activity; that substitution reverses stay-at-home habit and pulls retail footfall up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 12.4 to 11.4 while PARKS rose -33.9 to -20.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS rises at least 5 points and RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point simultaneously, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an explicit reopening regime, defined by PARKS above -25 and TRANSIT above -40 at the same time, capacity caps and travel advisories are lifted jointly, so retail capacity expands and the forward 28-day mean exceeds the trailing mean; the mechanism is dormant under tightening rules.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean > -25 AND TRANSIT weekly mean > -40 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w PARKS is -20.6 and TRANSIT is -37.1, satisfying both regime conditions
failure_condition: In weeks satisfying PARKS > -25 and TRANSIT > -40, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains 11.4 points above baseline, evidencing persistent work-from-home, while WORKPLACES is still -25.3; because discretionary retail in this metro is commuter-corridor weighted, elevated residential time diverts spend away from retail and caps the recovery.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 points for three consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been above +11 in all four weeks while WORKPLACES never exceeded -25.3
failure_condition: The 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -40.03 despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +10 points for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES improvement (-31.7 to -25.3) restores weekday commuter presence, and commuter presence is the primary predictor of weekday retail footfall, so retail recovers with a four-week lag as office attendance stabilises at a higher level.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved every week from -31.7 at t-3w to -25.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady reopening with rising office attendance
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES has improved for three consecutive weekly means, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM convergence toward baseline (-12.0 to -5.7) shows that stockpiling and one-trip-only shopping rules have ended and normal shopping circuits are restored; this normalization transmits into discretionary retail within one week, raising the immediate forward mean.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -12.0 at t-3w to -5.7 at t-0w, now within 6 points of baseline
failure_condition: In the week after GROCERY_PHARM prints within 2 points of baseline, the following one-week RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the current one-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal warming lifts PARKS first (-50.3 to -20.6), and the same weather shift that drives park visits drives outdoor-adjacent and high-street retail; the effect is amplified when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are also recovering, accelerating RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises at least 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped +13.3 points from t-1w to t-0w while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES also improved
failure_condition: When PARKS rises at least 10 points week-on-week while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both rising, the next two-week RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the prior two-week mean.
